Referee's correction to two failed attempts: a source PINNED AT EVERY LEVEL is not a conditioning of the stationary Gaussian at one time; the pinned process has stationary mean alpha G(y)/G(0) with G = (I - P)^-1. Executed (simulator probes/lib/formation_response.py): the nonlinear sphere law's potential around a persistent field source is 0.96-0.99 of (h/beta) x the lattice Green function, symmetric. TASK: (a) for the linear process with two sites pinned at every level to values a and b at distance r, compute the stationary law's cost: the large-deviation rate per level (the probability that the unpinned process stays within the pins), as a function of r; its sign for like and unlike pins; the coefficient of 1/r; (b) the same for two FIELD sources h_1, h_2 (no pinning): the change of the stationary mean and of the rate; is there an 'interaction energy' at all for a non-equilibrium process, and what replaces it (the rate function, or -log pi for the reversible law: compute both and compare); (c) superposition at linear order and the first nonlinear correction in 1/beta. Verify on L = 6..16 tori exactly. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/persistent-sources/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/persistent-sources/<name>/check.py"
